rubric.trivial: No behavior change: documentation, comments, wording, formatting, or repository housekeeping. Runs code_writer only.
rubric.light: A focused behavior change in one area, where the request itself states the check or the test to write, or where existing tests already cover it (including behavior-preserving refactors).
rubric.standard: New behavior, or a behavior change whose correctness needs new tests that the request does not spell out. Adds test_generator.
rubric.substantial: Touches security-sensitive behavior (authentication, secrets, sandboxing, permissions, personal data, bounds on untrusted input) or needs coordinated changes across several modules. Adds security_auditor.
rubric.architectural: Creates or restructures a subsystem, protocol, storage layer, or the pipeline orchestration itself. Same stages as substantial.

scoring_note: substantial and architectural compile to the same stages and reserve, so the routing score treats them as one route (heavy).
label_status: golden-* rows are owner labels; every other row is a draft label by Claude and needs owner review before it is used as ground truth. Owner decisions 2026-09-25: stage needs replace tiers; broader security review is preferred.

rows.request: The POST /session endpoint accepts requests with any Content-Type, but the body is always read from query parameters, and clients keep sending JSON bodies that get ignored. Make the API contract explicit: POST /session must require a Content-Type of application/json. When the header is missing or names any other type, answer 415 Unsupported Media Type with a short plain-text message and do not touch the store. GET requests are unaffected. Missing Content-Type on POST is also a 415 (no sniffing, no defaults).
rows.source: tests/evals/taskset-v0/tasks/content-type-enforcement.json (claude-draft label); security_review relabeled True by owner policy 2026-09-25 (an extra audit is acceptable; broader review is preferred)

rows.request: Store.Create in session.go currently overwrites an existing session when the same id is used twice. Change Create to return (Session, error): if the id already exists and has not expired, return the existing session unchanged together with a non-nil error (define ErrConflict for this). An expired session with the same id must be replaceable and must not return an error. Keep Get working exactly as before. Update main.go's call site so it still compiles and returns 409 Conflict on the error.
rows.source: tests/evals/taskset-v0/tasks/create-conflict-error.json (claude-draft label); security_review relabeled True by owner policy 2026-09-25 (an extra audit is acceptable; broader review is preferred)

rows.request: A runaway client can hammer POST /session with the same id. Add per-id rate limiting in main.go: implement func allowCreate(id string, now time.Time) bool backed by a package-level map guarded by a mutex that records the last ACCEPTED create time per id; a POST for an id that was accepted less than 1 second ago must be refused with 429 Too Many Requests and must not touch the store. Allowed requests proceed exactly as before. The limiter must be safe for concurrent use and must not rate-limit different ids independently of each other (each id has its own window).
rows.source: tests/evals/taskset-v0/tasks/create-rate-limit.json (claude-draft label)

The refactoring must not change any behavior: Get still reports expired sessions as not found and still drops them. Add nothing else; this is a pure extract-method refactor so later changes have one place to touch.
rows.source: tests/evals/taskset-v0/tasks/expiry-predicate-single-source.json (claude-draft label)

rows.request: Expiry behavior has regressed twice this quarter and nothing pins it. Write a regression test file named expiry_regression_test.go (package main) containing a single table-driven test func TestExpiryRegressionTable(t *testing.T) that covers ALL of these cases against a store with a 1-minute TTL and a controllable clock (store.now): (1) fresh session readable immediately; (2) session at exactly ttl is still live; (3) session one second past ttl returns ErrNotFound; (4) expired session is dropped by the read so Len reports one fewer; (5) a session created after an expired one with the same id is readable. Use errors.Is for error checks. The test must pass, and every case must be a table entry, not a separate test function.
rows.source: tests/evals/taskset-v0/tasks/expiry-regression-table.json (claude-draft label)

Extend GET /session in main.go with an optional query parameter fields: when fields=user, respond with only {"user": ...} from the session; when fields=id, only {"id": ...}; when the parameter is absent or has any other value, respond with the full session as today. A comma list like fields=id,user returns both keys. Field names are case-sensitive lowercase. Do not change session.go. Malformed requests keep their current behavior.

rows.request: Session data is user PII; GET /session currently serves it to anyone who can guess an id. Compare with subtle.ConstantTimeCompare from crypto/subtle (do not use ==). A missing or wrong token answers 401 Unauthorized. POST /session stays open (registration is unauthenticated by design). Do not change session.go.

rows.request: Store.Get in session.go currently refreshes LastSeen on every read, so polling the /session endpoint keeps a session alive forever. Change Get to be read-only: it must report the session as expired when now-LastSeen exceeds ttl, but it must NOT update LastSeen. Add a new Touch(id) error method that explicitly refreshes LastSeen (unknown id returns ErrNotFound). Update main.go: the GET /session handler must call Get (no refresh), and add a POST /session/touch handler that calls Touch and answers 204, or 404 when Touch returns ErrNotFound.
rows.source: tests/evals/taskset-v0/tasks/get-no-refresh.json (claude-draft label); security_review relabeled True by owner policy 2026-09-25 (an extra audit is acceptable; broader review is preferred)

rows.request: Several callers implement get-or-create by calling Get then Create, which is racy: two callers can both miss and both create. Add func (s *Store) GetOrCreate(id, user string) (Session, bool) to session.go. It must be ATOMIC (one lock acquisition): if a live session with id exists, return it and false (wasCreated); otherwise create it with the caller's user and return it with true. An expired session is replaced and true is returned. Do not implement this by calling Get and Create; do the lookup and insert inside a single lock scope.
rows.source: tests/evals/taskset-v0/tasks/get-or-create.json (claude-draft label); security_review relabeled True by owner policy 2026-09-25 (an extra audit is acceptable; broader review is preferred)
